title: NEB Class 11 English — Grammar — 2021
origin: curated NEB-pattern set filling the 2021 gap for class-11 grammar

questions.question: Rewrite as conditional sentences: (a) He didn't study. He failed. (third conditional) (b) It rains. The match is cancelled. (first conditional)
questions.solution:
(a) Past regret takes the third conditional — if + past perfect, would have + past participle: 'If he had studied, he would not have failed.' (Both clauses step one tense back from reality.)
(b) A real future possibility takes the first conditional — if + present simple, will + verb: 'If it rains, the match will be cancelled.'

questions.question: Fill in the blanks with articles (a/an/the/×): (a) ___ Mount Everest is ___ highest peak in ___ world. (b) She plays ___ guitar and ___ football.
questions.solution:
(a) 'Mount Everest is the highest peak in the world.' — no article before Mount Everest (named mountain, zero article); 'the highest' (superlative takes the); 'the world' (unique object takes the).
(b) 'She plays the guitar and × football.' — instruments take 'the' (the guitar), while games/sports take no article (football).

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag: 'You haven't seen my keys, ___?' (a) have you (b) haven't you (c) did you
questions.solution: (a) 'have you'. Tags reverse the statement's polarity: a negative statement ('haven't seen') takes a positive tag with the same auxiliary ('have you'). 'You haven't seen my keys, have you?'
